- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 80.5), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward by 1–2 points if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- If sentiment shows strong negative signals (≤ -0.2) in last 3–5 days, model overcorrects downward; avoid excessive downward bias; consider slight upward adjustment.
- Model consistently overestimates 30-day horizon by 0.5–1.5 points on average; apply a 0.75–1.0 offset to forecasted values for 30d horizon.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.4–0.6), model exhibits lagged response; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days or smooth transitions to avoid abrupt swings.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.2) over 5+ days, model underestimates; increase forecast by 0.5–1.0 to account for subdued market sentiment.
